title: BilboMD: a web-accessible SAXS and AlphaFold-guided modeling pipeline.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 18319542 metadata: a single code archive, bl1231/bilbomd-v2.4.6.zip, 73,054,874 bytes (over the 50 MB cap, not downloaded), CC-BY-4.0. GitHub repo bl1231/bilbomd top-level listing: application code plus an example-data folder with subfolders af, auto, crd, of3, pdb, sans, scoper (pipeline demo inputs, not a labelled table). The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles request timed out once at 120 s and was not retried.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the paper is a software/web-server description (molecular dynamics sampling plus SAXS (small-angle X-ray scattering) curve fitting with FoXS/MultiFoXS); that the case studies use only a handful of SASBDB (Small Angle Scattering Biological Data Bank) entries such as SASDVF2 and SASDNF2; that job metadata sits in a server-side database not released.

a1_downloadable.note: Only code is deposited (73 MB Zenodo zip, GitHub repo). No dataset accompanies the paper; job records live in a private server database.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table and no label column. Any target (for example a fit-quality score, chi-squared between model and SAXS curve) would have to be generated by running the pipeline yourself.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be SAXS curves and structures from SASBDB and PDB (Protein Data Bank), which belong to other resources; the repo's example-data holds only demo inputs.

a5_enough_rows.note: No labelled rows; the paper's case studies cover a few SASBDB entries.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: none released; generating labels needs GPU molecular dynamics
a6_fits_laptop.note: Nothing to load; producing labels would mean running molecular dynamics and AlphaFold, which the paper itself runs on NERSC (a supercomputing centre) GPUs.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any label from pipeline output (best-fit ensemble, chi-squared) is computed by FoXS/MultiFoXS from the features themselves, so training on it would distil the software (circular).

backbone.name: None applicable; AlphaFold appears only as a structure generator inside the pipeline

integration.partner_dataset: SASBDB, joinable to PDB/UniProt via entry metadata (not checked)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not applicable: this paper releases no data to join.

honest_claim_h3: No claim possible: the paper releases software, not a measured dataset.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a protein's predicted structure and its X-ray scattering curve to predict how well a flexible-ensemble model will fit the data.
plain_idea.train_on: Pairs of protein structure and solution scattering curve; number of examples unknown because no job database is released.
plain_idea.predict: The fit quality of the pipeline's best ensemble, which the software computes itself rather than a separate lab measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Beamline users could skip slow simulations for proteins unlikely to fit, but the label is the software's own output, so little biology would be learned.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. A real scattering-ML project would have to start from SASBDB itself, not from BilboMD.

effort.compute_note: Nothing to estimate: no dataset; generating labels would require GPU molecular dynamics per protein.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Already done: the Zenodo deposit is a single code zip and the GitHub repo has only demo inputs.

verdict_reason: Software/web-server paper with no released dataset or label column (A1, A2, A5 fail); any label would be the pipeline's own computed fit score (A8 circular).
